21034-the-corner-house-girls-at-school.title: The Corner House Girls At School
21034-the-corner-house-girls-at-school.creator: Barse & Co.
21034-the-corner-house-girls-at-school.description: A book by Barse & Co.. "We know Allie Neuman--Tess and me," ventured Dot, the youngest of the Corner House girls. "She lives on Willow Street beyond Mrs. Adams' house, and she is going to be in my grade at school."

66323-the-natural-history-of-the-gent.title: The Natural History Of The Gent
66323-the-natural-history-of-the-gent.creator: Unknown
66323-the-natural-history-of-the-gent.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. We were exceedingly delighted when we read this police report. We had laboured, for three or four years, to bring the race of Gents into universal contempt; and we at last found that an intelligent and respected London magistrate had publicly stated, from the bench, his opinion of the miserable class in question; and that it exactly coincided with our own.

arxiv-1903-04209.title: From interpretability to inference: an estimation framework for universal approximators Thanks: Disclaimer: The views expressed in this work are not necessarily those of the Bank of England or one of its committees. All errors are mine. Contact: Bank of England, Advanced Analytics Division (Threadne
arxiv-1903-04209.creator: Andreas Joseph
arxiv-1903-04209.description: Abstract We present a novel framework for estimation and inference with the broad class of universal approximators. Estimation is based on the decomposition of model predictions into Shapley values. Inference relies on analyzing the bias and variance properties of individual Shapley components.

arxiv-2105-12263.title: Temperature Damping of Magneto-Intersubband Resistance Oscillations in Magnetically Entangled Subbands
arxiv-2105-12263.creator: Sara Abedi, Sergey Vitkalov, A. A. Bykov, A. K. Bakarov
arxiv-2105-12263.description: Abstract Magneto-intersubband resistance oscillations (MISO) of highly mobile 2D electrons in symmetric GaAs quantum wells with two populated subbands are studied in magnetic fields tilted from the normal to the 2D electron layer at different temperatures T \displaystyle T . Decrease of MISO amplitude with temperature increase is observed.

arxiv-2110-15444.title: 10 Security and Privacy Problems in Large Foundation Models
arxiv-2110-15444.creator: Jinyuan Jia, Hongbin Liu, Neil Zhenqiang Gong
arxiv-2110-15444.description: Abstract Foundation models–such as GPT, CLIP, and DINO–have achieved revolutionary progress in the past several years and are commonly believed to be a promising approach for general-purpose AI. In particular, self-supervised learning is adopted to pre-train a foundation model using a large amount of unlabeled data. A pre-trained foundation model is like an “operating system” of the AI ecosystem.

arxiv-2112-12461.title: Spin-selective equilibration among integer quantum Hall edge channels
arxiv-2112-12461.creator: Giorgio Nicolí, Christoph Adam, Marc P. Röösli, Peter Märki, Jan Scharnetzky, Christian Reichl, Werner Wegscheider, Thomas M. Ihn, Klaus Ensslin
arxiv-2112-12461.description: Abstract The equilibration between quantum Hall edge modes is known to depend on the disorder potential and the steepness of the edge. Modern samples with higher mobilities and setups with lower electron temperatures call for a further exploration of the topic. We develop a framework to systematically measure and analyze the equilibration of many (up to 8) integer edge modes.

arxiv-2207-09356.title: Playing Mastermind on quantum computers The authors are ordered alphabetically.
arxiv-2207-09356.creator: Lvzhou Li, Jingquan Luo, Yongzhen Xu
arxiv-2207-09356.description: Abstract From the 1970s up to now, the classic two-player game, Mastermind, has attracted plenty of attention, not only from the public as a popular game, but also from the academic community as a scientific issue. Mastermind with n n positions and k k colors is formally described as follows.

arxiv-2211-01065.title: Soft-Output Signal Detection for Cetacean Vocalizations Using Spectral Entropy, K-Means Clustering and the Continuous Wavelet Transform Journal: Ecological Informatics
arxiv-2211-01065.creator: M.W. Rademan, D.J.J. Versfeld, J.A. du Preez
arxiv-2211-01065.description: Abstract Underwater passive acoustic monitoring systems record many hours of audio data for marine research, making fast and reliable non-causal signal detection paramount. Such detectors assist in reducing the amount of labor required for signal annotations, which often contain large portions devoid of signals. Cetacean vocalization detection based on spectral entropy is investigated as a means of vocalization discovery.

arxiv-2211-02657.title: MolE: a molecular foundation model for drug discovery
arxiv-2211-02657.creator: Oscar Méndez-Lucio, Christos Nicolaou, Berton Earnshaw
arxiv-2211-02657.description: Abstract Models that accurately predict properties based on chemical structure are valuable tools in drug discovery. However, for many properties, public and private training sets are typically small, and it is difficult for the models to generalize well outside of the training data.

arxiv-2302-03848.title: Controlling Personality Style in Dialogue with Zero-Shot Prompt-Based Learning
arxiv-2302-03848.creator: Angela Ramirez, Mamon Alsalihy, Kartik Aggarwal, Cecilia Li, Liren Wu, and Marilyn Walker
arxiv-2302-03848.description: Abstract Prompt-based or in-context learning has been shown to achieve high zero-shot performance on many natural language generation (NLG) tasks. Here we explore the performance of prompt-based learning for simultaneously controlling the personality and the semantic accuracy of an NLG for task-oriented dialogue.

arxiv-2307-12058.title: Discovering Spatio-Temporal Rationales for Video Question Answering
arxiv-2307-12058.creator: Yicong Li, Junbin Xiao, Chun Feng, Xiang Wang, Tat-Seng Chua
arxiv-2307-12058.description: Abstract This paper strives to solve complex video question answering (VideoQA) which features long video containing multiple objects and events at different time. To tackle the challenge, we highlight the importance of identifying question-critical temporal moments and spatial objects from the vast amount of video content.

arxiv-2411-07447.title: Saving GPU Hours in LLM Inference System Development and Online Workloads with Simulation and DBMS-Inspired Cache Replacement Policies
arxiv-2411-07447.creator: Kyoungmin Kim, Jiacheng Li, Kijae Hong, Qunyou Liu, Darong Huang, Anastasia Ailamaki
arxiv-2411-07447.description: Abstract LLMs are increasingly used world-wide from daily tasks to agentic systems and data analytics, requiring significant GPU resources. While LLM inference systems are capable of serving millions of requests from multiple users, they often lack theoretical models to determine whether they achieve the performance upper bounds of underlying hardware resources.

arxiv-2508-08931.title: Superheavy Q-Balls and Cosmology
arxiv-2508-08931.creator: John McDonald
arxiv-2508-08931.description: Abstract We propose a model for the cosmological formation of superheavy Q-Balls in the mass range 10 − 7 ​ M ⊙ 10^{-7}\,M_{\odot} to 10 6 ​ M ⊙ 10^{6}\,M_{\odot} . The model is based on a hidden sector scalar potential motivated by broken scale invariance, for which analytic Q-ball solutions and numerical simulations of condensate fragmentation exist.

arxiv-2511-16853.title: Towards Unified Vision Language Models for Forest Ecological Analysis in Earth Observation
arxiv-2511-16853.creator: Xizhe Xue, Xiao Xiang Zhu
arxiv-2511-16853.description: Abstract Recent progress in vision language models (VLMs) has enabled remarkable perception and reasoning capabilities, yet their potential for scientific regression in Earth Observation (EO) remains largely unexplored. Existing EO datasets mainly emphasize semantic understanding tasks such as captioning or classification, lacking benchmarks that align multimodal perception with measurable biophysical variables.

pmc-10558554.title: Topologically crafted spatiotemporal vortices in acoustics
pmc-10558554.creator: Hongliang Zhang, Yeyang Sun, Junyi Huang, Bingjun Wu, Zhaoju Yang, Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Zhichao Ruan
pmc-10558554.description: Vortices in fluids and gases have piqued the human interest for centuries. Development of classical-wave physics and quantum mechanics highlighted wave vortices characterized by phase singularities and topological charges. In particular, vortex beams have found numerous applications in modern optics and other areas. Recently, optical spatiotemporal vortex states exhibiting the phase singularity both in space and time have been described.

pmc-10740885.title: Oncostatin M’s Involvement in the Pathogenesis of Chronic Rhinosinusitis: Focus on Type 1 and 2 Inflammation
pmc-10740885.creator: Chie Ishikawa, Sachio Takeno, Yukako Okamoto, Tomohiro Kawasumi, Takashi Kakimoto, Kota Takemoto, Manabu Nishida, Takashi Ishino, Takao Hamamoto, Tsutomu Ueda, Akio Tanaka, Giuseppe Guida, Cristiano Caruso
pmc-10740885.description: Objectives: The cytokine oncostatin M (OSM) elicits pathogenic effects involving disruption of the epithelial barrier function as a part of immunological response networks. It is unclear how these integrated cytokine signals influence inflammation and other physiological processes in the pathology of chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS).

pmc-11336113.title: Optimal routing and end-to-end entanglement distribution in quantum networks
pmc-11336113.creator: Joy Halder, Akhmadjon Rajabov, Riccardo Bassoli, Frank H P Fitzek, Gerhard P Fettweis
pmc-11336113.description: Quantum networks are designed to transmit quantum bits (qubits) among quantum devices to enable new network resources for the applications. Entanglement distribution and entanglement swapping are fundamental procedures that are required in several network operations. However, they are probabilistic operations, which can lead to severe network performance degradation.

pmc-11359613.title: Order–Disorder Transition in Rutile VO2(M) Electrodes during Li Intercalation and Extraction
pmc-11359613.creator: Morten Johansen, Dorthe B Ravnsbæk
pmc-11359613.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Transition metal oxides are widely employed as electrode materials in Li-ion batteries. During battery operation, Li ions are intercalated and extracted from the framework of the electrode structure, causing structural transitions. In some materials, the process can drive order–disorder transitions; however, insights into such processes are generally lacking, although they are essential for our understanding of battery aging and in the design of new sustainable battery chemistries.

pmc-11607666.title: Delivering therapeutic RNA into the brain using extracellular vesicles
pmc-11607666.creator: Paniz Shirmast, Mahdi Abedinzadeh Shahri, Austin Brent, Adi Idris, Nigel A.J. McMillan
pmc-11607666.description: RNA science has experienced a surge, particularly its application to vaccine and therapeutic development. Delivery of RNA molecules into the brain remains one of the biggest therapeutic challenges with the blood-brain barrier excluding most drug-delivery modalities such as lipid nanoparticles.

Pers (synonym: Helianthemum rubellum C. Presl.

pmc-12448257.title: The Development and Growth of the English National Real-Time Syndromic Surveillance Program: Key Developments and Lessons Learned From the First Two Decades
pmc-12448257.creator: Gillian E Smith, Natalia R Jones, Sally E Harcourt, Sue Smith, Paul Loveridge, Roger A Morbey, Helen E Hughes, Obaghe Edeghere, Daniel Todkill, Sue Ibbotson, Duncan Cooper, Brian McCloskey, Alex J Elliot, Jiban Khuntia
pmc-12448257.description: Syndromic surveillance now forms an integral part of the surveillance for a wide range of hazards in many countries. Establishing syndromic surveillance systems can be difficult due to the many different sources of data that can be used, cost pressures, the importance of data security, and the presence of different (and rapidly evolving) technologies.

pmc-13284737.title: Choroid plexus remodeling linked to impaired CSF‐mediated clearance and Alzheimer's disease progression
pmc-13284737.creator: Haolin Yin, Yuepeng Deng, ZiHao Lu, Yu Jiang, Chao Zuo, Jianyu Li, Linlin Guo, Binwu Ying, Giuseppe Battaglia, Xiaohe Tian, Qiyong Gong, for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI)
pmc-13284737.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). INTRODUCTIONImpaired cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) ‐mediated clearance has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but how choroid plexus (ChP) remodeling relates to these processes in vivo remains incompletely understood.METHODSIn a large ADNI cohort, we integrated structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), amyloid/tau positron emission tomography (PET), and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) ‐derived analysis along the perivascular space (ALPS) to characterize ChP changes and their associations with ventricular measures, glymphatic marker, CSF biomarkers, and cognition across diagnostic stages.

pmc-13437672.title: Biomechanics and Oxidative Stress: An Integrative Review of the Redox–Mechanobiological Axis and the Role of Trace Elements in Disease
pmc-13437672.creator: Servet Kavak
pmc-13437672.description: Oxidative stress and mechanobiological signaling are increasingly recognized as interconnected determinants of cellular and systemic homeostasis. Reactive oxygen species (ROS), traditionally associated with molecular damage, are now understood to directly regulate cytoskeletal remodeling, membrane viscoelasticity, mitochondrial dynamics, and mechanotransduction pathways including focal adhesion kinase (FAK), integrins, and Yes-associated protein/transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (YAP/TAZ).

uslaw-usc-t15-s6753.title: 15 U.S.C. § 6753 — Membership
uslaw-usc-t15-s6753.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s6753.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 93 (Insurance); Subchapter III (National Association Of Registered Agents And Brokers). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Eligibility (1) In general Any insurance producer licensed in its home State shall, subject to paragraphs (2) and (4), be eligible to become a member of the Association. (2) Ineligibility for suspension or revocation of license.
